title: Persist expenses with SwiftData
prompt: Make `Expense` a SwiftData model and finish the list: it must fetch expenses newest first, delete the ones the user swipes away, and add a coffee expense when the button is tapped. The app's scene already has `.modelContainer(for: Expense.self)`.
hints: The macro that makes a class persistent is named after what it describes.
The property wrapper that fetches models for a view is also the name of a database read.
All writes go through the model context: one method adds a new model, another removes an existing one.
explanation: `@Model` turns the class into a persisted SwiftData model. `@Query(sort: \Expense.date, order: .reverse)` fetches every expense newest first and refreshes when the data changes. Writes go through the context from the environment: `context.delete(_:)` removes a model and `context.insert(_:)` adds one. The main context autosaves, and the query updates the list on its own, so there's no array to keep in sync by hand.
